tagline: North out of Clarksville, along the ridges to the Buffalo.
intro: Highway 21 leaves US 64 at Clarksville and heads north into the Ozark National Forest, up into the Boston Mountains. For 35 miles it keeps to the ridges between the headwaters of major streams, and it is a main way in to the Ozark Highlands Trail.
The Boston Mountains have several stories for their name, and apparently none of them involve Massachusetts. The drive ends at the Buffalo, the first river in the country to be made a National River.

moments.title: Ozone
moments.text: Eleven and a half miles north of Clarksville, Ozone counted 92 people in 2020 and still keeps a post office of its own.

moments.title: Mossville
moments.text: Over the Newton County line the highway passes Mossville, a community standing at 2,267 feet.

moments.title: Boxley
moments.text: Highway 21 meets the upper Buffalo at Boxley Bridge. ARDOT says to watch for elk here, and the park keeps the only herd in the state.

sources.label: Arkansas Tourism, Road Trip: The Scenic Byway Guide to Northwest Arkansas
